content:
## Source
.design/m5/49-hardware-token-signing.md — AC-5, AC-7 + decomposition PR 10.

## Surface
- CI gate: `cargo +nightly miri test -p polaris-signer --test signer_audit` runs and passes.
- Audit script: `polaris-signer/tests/audit_no_key_exfil.rs` — uses strace (or platform equivalent) to record syscalls during a softhsm2 sign session; greps for any `write()` carrying key bytes outside the PKCS#11 transport. Fails on any hit.
- PIN-secrecy audit: `polaris-signer/tests/audit_pin_secrecy.rs` — runs the daemon, takes a memory snapshot (procfs `/proc/<pid>/maps`), greps for plaintext PIN. Fails on a hit (best-effort; documented as "memory hygiene under best-effort limits").

## Rust-quality notes
- Per rust-quality §5: this is the unsafe-discipline closure for the hwtoken epic.
- The strace audit is platform-specific (Linux). Mark with `cfg!(target_os = "linux")` skip otherwise.
- The PIN memory audit is best-effort — `secrecy::SecretString` makes it harder, not impossible, to leak via syscall traces. Document this limitation in the test file.
- miri may not have full support for some of the FFI paths in `cryptoki` — if so, miri runs on a tonic-client unit subset, with the FFI exercise documented as "manually audited."

## External references
- miri docs: https://github.com/rust-lang/miri
- strace audit patterns: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man1/strace.1.html
- `procfs` memory inspection: https://docs.kernel.org/filesystems/proc.html

## Acceptance (AC-5, AC-7)
- [ ] AC-5: strace audit confirms no `write()` syscall outside PKCS#11 transport carries key bytes during sign.
- [ ] AC-7: PIN memory audit (best-effort) finds no plaintext PIN in daemon process memory.
- [ ] miri job runs on the daemon's library code; FFI exercises documented as manually-audited if miri can't cover them.

## Blocks / blocked-by
- Blocked by #172.
- Closes the hardware-token epic. On approval, close #153 with `--kind result`.
